A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TISER study. Their complete main text, algorithms, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite layout changes and added appendices.

before.justification: Sections 3.2–3.4 report original prompting and fine-tuning experiments, out-of-distribution evaluations, and component ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds measured output-token usage in Appendix J.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 adds explicit repeat, reasoning-update, and stopping lines. However, v1's Appendix C, step 4, already instructed the model to repeat reasoning when necessary, and that prompt is unchanged. The revision clarifies the existing iterative procedure; dataset construction and LoRA training remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use TGQA, TempReason L2/L3, TimeQA easy/hard, Test-of-Time, and MultiHopRAG. The added reasoning example and token analysis establish no additional dataset, domain, or distinct task scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–5 is unchanged, including T5-large, Temp-T5, REMEMO-large, TG-LLM, and the closed/open model comparisons. The token analysis compares the already-used standard and TISER prompting strategies.

E3.justification: Appendix J introduces an evaluation of average output tokens per response and per reasoning stage. Existing benchmark splits, EM/F1 metrics, model configurations, and training settings remain unchanged. The new token analysis leaves its precise model, test sample, and counting procedure unspecified.

E4.justification: New Appendix H illustrates DeepSeek V2.5 correcting an erroneous event ordering over two reasoning rounds. Appendix J adds a computational-overhead analysis. Existing component ablations, training-subset comparisons, and correct/incorrect reasoning examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new token averages are reported without uncertainty and do not introduce a different statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–9 retain their numerical results. New Table 10 reports 3.41 versus 94.74 average tokens for standard versus TISER prompting, with stage averages of 30.27, 23.62, and 49.02. Appendix H adds a successful multi-round correction example. Appendix J also adds a '+38.3%' accuracy summary that is not reconciled with Table 1.

T1.justification: No mathematical definitions, assumptions, theoretical results, proofs, or derivations are added or revised. Algorithm 1's explicit loop documents iteration already specified in the existing prompt.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims: timeline-based self-reflection, synthetic reasoning data, improved temporal reasoning, competitive small-model performance, and out-of-distribution transfer.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations and limitations concerning computational overhead, dependence on reasoning-trace datasets, and text-only applicability are retained. Appendix J quantifies the previously stated cost–accuracy tradeoff without introducing a distinct interpretation or applicability boundary.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-and-data availability statement with a repository link and direct access links for the five existing benchmarks. The detailed fine-tuning appendix moves from H to I with unchanged content; no new training hyperparameters or hardware details are supplied.

R1.justification: The references and related-work discussion are unchanged, including the claimed novelty of applying test-time scaling and self-reflection to temporal reasoning. New resource links provide access information rather than additional research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 expands the pseudocode, adds resource footnotes and Appendices H and J, and updates the fine-tuning appendix reference to I. The existing prose and main section organization are largely unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds a boxed multi-round example and Table 10, expands Algorithm 1's display, and reflows existing material, including relocating Table 1 and Algorithm 2. Figure 1 and the structures of Tables 1–9 are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves clarity and reproducibility through explicit iterative pseudocode, an illustrative multi-round example, and code/data access information. The new cost analysis has unresolved inconsistencies: its stage averages total 102.91 tokens versus 94.74 overall, and its '+38.3%' statement does not match Table 1's relevant Qwen comparison, 52.3% to 91.1% EM. These weaknesses limit the benefit; the core empirical evidence remains unchanged.
